story_type: HALO freefall jump from a C-17 at 20,000 feet, helmet cameras, canopy opens low, landing
hook: They stepped off a C-17 at twenty thousand feet.
narration: These airmen stepped off the back of a C-17, twenty thousand feet above the ground.
They're from the 19th Aerospace Medicine Squadron, and this is a HALO jump.
HALO means high altitude, low opening. Jump very high, fall most of the way, and open the parachute late.
Up there the air is too thin to breathe for long, so every jumper wears an oxygen mask.
Then the door opens, and one by one, they step out into the sky.
They fall face down, arms and legs spread, to stay stable.
The farms and runways below grow bigger every second.
Only much lower does the parachute finally open.
outcome: The canopy opened, and the jumper rode it all the way down to a landing in the grass.
title: HALO jump from 20,000 feet
description:
Airmen from the 19th Aerospace Medicine Squadron's High Altitude Airdrop Mission Support unit make high altitude, low opening (HALO) jumps from a C-17 at 12,000 and 20,000 feet at Charleston Air Force Base, South Carolina, in May 2019.
